results.fact: Length of the rappel below the summit
results.correct_value: A short (~50-60 ft) rappel off a tree anchor; the 100-150 ft figure is the rope length, not the rappel length
results.evidence: The published route description reports parties rope up for one short pitch, rappel it off the same tree, used a 150 ft rope for climb and rappel and say anything over 100 ft of rope is adequate - i.e. 100-150 ft is a ROPE length, and a doubled 100 ft rope implies a rappel of roughly 50 ft. The row's rappels, detailed_rack, pitch_detail, gear and rope_note all put the step at ~50-75 ft; the waypoint note and descent_text turned the rope length into a rappel length. No second independent external source describes the step, so this rests on the row plus one external source.

results.fact: Which summit(s) the climbing day actually reaches
results.correct_value: Day 2 climbs the 5,814' main summit via the notch and short roped step, not the Middle and North Peaks
results.evidence: The published route page for Sheep Gap Mountain describes the main summit as reached from Weden Pass via a traverse to a notch with one roped pitch that is rappelled off a tree, and separately notes that the north summit (Pt 5683) is a quick class 2/3 scramble west of Weden Pass for those who do NOT want the main summit. Peakbagger lists Sheep Gap Mountain (main) and Sheep Gap Mountain-North Peak as separate summits, and an October 2024 trip report titled for the North and Middle Peaks records a high point of 5,683 ft - i.e. the itinerary copied a trip that never reached this route's 5,814 ft summit.

results.fact: Total elevation loss for the trip
results.evidence: loss_ft 3452 equals exactly the net relief from the trailhead (2,362 ft) to the summit (5,814 ft), so it is a different quantity from the itinerary's cumulative 4,300 ft, not a typo. No external source gives a car-to-car cumulative gain/loss for the main summit (the only measured report went to the 5,683 ft North/Middle peaks), and the catalog has refused setting loss = gain by out-and-back arithmetic as a class, so no patch.

results.fact: Whether October is within season for this route
results.evidence: season (Jul-Sep), best_season, climate and seasonal_guidance's own October entry ('risky', 'end of best-season window') all put October outside the reliable window; optimalWindow alone extended it to October. A Gothic Basin approach guide gives late July to early September as the prime window.

results.evidence: The row's waypoints (summit at 5.9 mi) and itinerary give ~11.8 mi round trip, but the only measured external figure, a 2024 trip to the North and Middle peaks via Weden Pass, logged 13.8 mi round trip, which supports partner_requirements' 13-14 mi rather than the itinerary. With one external source that disagrees with the majority of fields and no second source for the main summit, no patch.

results.fact: Total elevation gain and loss for the Southwest Route
results.evidence: External figures do not isolate this route: the best-documented trip logged ~34 mi and 14,000 ft gained and lost over six days but included Gunsight Peak; a route description gives ~5,500 ft of gain from the trailhead to Itswoot Ridge alone, which with a summit day that crosses the Dome-Chickamin col twice implies well over the itinerary's 8,200 ft. The itinerary's own sums (gain 8,200, loss 8,400) do not balance for a round trip either, so neither gain_ft/loss_ft nor the itinerary can be confirmed; no patch.

results.fact: Hardest rock grade on the standard ascent line
results.correct_value: Class 3 (south-side gully Class 3, upper west ridge Class 2-3); Class 3-4 applies only to the optional lower west ridge descent
results.evidence: One party's account rates the steep south gully Class 3 with an easy Class 2 romp from the ridge notch to the summit; another describes the upper west ridge as a Class 2-3 scramble and reserves Class 3-4 for the optional lower west ridge descent; the peak's encyclopedia entry gives the easiest route as a Class 3 scramble, and a third party rates the direct ridge from the col Class 3+. None rates the standard gully/west ridge line Class 4.

results.correct_value: Normally in condition July through September (Jul-Sep); spring ascents are snow climbs
results.evidence: Documented ascents of the standard line fall in late June-early July, and route notes warn the bergschrund at the Dome-Sinister col opens later in the season, making September marginal - matching the Jul-Sep chip, itinerary.cal and seasonal_guidance. A May ascent is recorded but only as a snow climb that bypassed the normal route on a snow ramp, which is why itinerary.cal already frames May-June as ski-mountaineering; no source supports October.
